title: Matrix-driven pathways enabling complete defluorination of 6 : 2 FTCA in simulated alkaline IEX regeneration wastewater: comparison of UV/S and UV/PS with mechanistic and kinetic insights
content: Management of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) in concentrated ion exchange still bottoms is an emerging focus, particularly the integration of destructive technologies with well-established removal techniques. This study, for the first time, evaluates the effectiveness of (1) ultraviolet/sulfite (UV/S) and (2) UV/persulfate (UV/PS) in degradation and defluorination of 6 : 2 fluorotelomer carboxylic acid (6 : 2 FTCA) in various simulated ion exchange (IEX) regeneration still bottoms. Treating NaOH containing waste, 100% defluorination was achieved through UV/S treatment, as compared to 52.6% with UV/PS. Mechanistic assessment of the process confirmed that within NaOH containing wastes, 6 : 2 FTCA undergoes rapid conversion to fluorotelomer unsaturated acid (6 : 2 FTUA), which degrades via ˙OH attack and fluoride release to perfluoroalkyl carboxylic acids (PFCAs). While no PFCA degradation was achieved in the UV/PS treatment, UV/S treatment was effective in complete PFCA defluorination through eaq− attack, aligned with calculations from the comprehensive kinetic modeling. Overall, this work highlights the feasibility of complete 6 : 2 FTCA defluorination in NaOH containing simulated IEX regeneration waste through integrated removal and destructive technologies with relevant availability of ˙OH and eaq−.
